claim: former_names: ['PINACLE Express (lighter-weight operator tier referenced in PINACLE Mobile listing)']
finding: PINACLE Express is a current operator tier, not a former name: the PINACLE Mobile App Store description (v3.11.0, Oct 24 2026) offers the app to both PINACLE and PINACLE Express operators.
resolution: former_names: []; PINACLE Express noted as a current lighter operator tier in extra.

claim: former_names: 'PNC Popmoney (legacy P2P, pre-Zelle; not referenced on current site - INFERRED from industry history)'
finding: PNC's own 'Popmoney to Zelle' page still exists and states Popmoney was discontinued nationwide by its provider and removed from PNC Online Banking on June 24, 2023; its comparison table shows Zelle in the Mobile app only. The former name is CONFIRMED_BANK, not INFERRED, and the page explains why PNC has no web P2P.
resolution: PNC Popmoney (Online Banking P2P; discontinued and removed June 24, 2023) - CONFIRMED_BANK [S951].

claim: network_or_vendor: '... Visa/Mastercard (push-to-card, scheme unnamed) ...'; PNC-P14-S04 Direct to Debit Card network not named
finding: PNC's Oct 29 2025 press release names Visa Direct as the rail for its immediate push-to-card capability and says Direct to Debit Card is available via API and ePayments. There is no Mastercard Send reference; the ePayments schedule itself says 'Direct to Debit (Visa®)'.
resolution: Visa Direct is the push-to-card rail for Direct to Debit Card (API and ePayments).

claim: (absent) PNC-Visa Direct collaboration
finding: The chapter's recent changes omit the Oct 29 2025 PNC-Visa announcement, which expands immediate push-to-card disbursements (insurance, gig, EWA, refunds) for Treasury Management clients. It came eight days after FedNow.
resolution: Add 2025-10-29 PNC-Visa Direct collaboration to recent changes.

claim: PNC Mobile app ... 'new app experience' rolled out in phases from v5.4.0, 2025-2026
finding: On a re-read of the App Store Version History DOM (each note is paired with its version in the same list item), the phased-rollout sentence first appears on 5.0.0 (2026-05-15). The rollout ran in 2026 only, not 2025-2026.
resolution: PNC Mobile app ('new app experience' rolled out in phases May-Sep 2026, v5.0.0-v5.4.1; current v5.7.0).

claim: 2025-2026: PNC Mobile 'new app experience' released in phases from v5.4.0; v5.6.1 live Nov 2026
finding: The phased rollout started with v5.0.0 (May 15 2026). v5.6.1 shipped Oct 27 2026, and v5.7.0 is the current build (Nov 5 2026).
resolution: Single corrected line replaces recent_changes[1] and [5].

claim: Correction: phased rollout started with 5.0.0/5.1.0 (May 15-Jun 9, 2026), not 5.4.0; the 'released in phases' note disappeared at 5.6.0 (Oct 14, 2026); 5.7.0 shipped ~Nov 5, 2026
finding: The gap-fill table shifted release notes by one row. In the DOM the phased note is on 5.0.0 through 5.4.1 and missing from 5.5.0 (Sep 23 2026) onward. 5.1.0 is dated Jun 10, not Jun 9. The 5.7.0 date is right.
resolution: Phased note on v5.0.0-v5.4.1; dropped from v5.5.0 (Sep 23 2026).

claim: App 4.63 (Apr 2, 2026): push notifications for all available PNC alerts; app 4.61.1 (Dec 18, 2025): 24/7 debit card lock/unlock
finding: Same one-row shift. 'Push notifications for all available PNC alerts' is the 4.62 note (Feb 10 2026), and 4.63 (Apr 2 2026) is a generic UX release. '24/7 debit card lock/unlock' is the 4.61 note (Dec 4 2025), and 4.61.1 (Dec 18 2025) is generic.
resolution: App 4.62 (Feb 10, 2026): push notifications for all PNC alerts; App 4.61 (Dec 4, 2025): 24/7 debit card lock/unlock.

claim: The phased 'new app experience' (v5.4+) has drawn negative App Store reviews ...
finding: The new experience is v5.0+ (May 2026), not v5.4+.
resolution: '(v5.0+, rolled out May-Sep 2026)'.

claim: Scheduled and recurring Zelle payments exist (CONFIRMED_BANK, S017); editable until 11:59 PM ET the day before
finding: Only the Zelle Terms of Use (v2.7, Feb 2026, s.9) mention future-dated and recurring Zelle payments. The consumer Guide to Using Zelle and the Zelle page describe no schedule option, and PNC's Popmoney-to-Zelle page says Zelle does not offer future-dated or recurring payments. That page is undated and probably dates from 2023, but it is still live. Two bank sources disagree.
resolution: Keep the sub-product. Add an open question: 'Does the PNC Mobile app expose future-dated/recurring Zelle (Terms v2.7 s.9) given the popmoney-to-zelle page says it does not?' An authenticated app session or a current PNC FAQ would settle it.

claim: capabilities.scam_warning_interstitial: true
finding: No public PNC page, video or PDF shows an in-flow scam interstitial. The researcher's own open_questions say the wording 'requires an authenticated session'. Marketing copy ('only send money to people you know and trust') and terms are not an in-flow interstitial, so 'true' is not supported.
resolution: scam_warning_interstitial = 'unknown' (4 sub-products); other_flags.scam_education_content = true.

claim: RTP credit transfers capped at $1,000,000 (other_flags.cap_usd 1000000)
finding: PNC's RTP page does say 'Currently limited to $1,000,000', but The Clearing House raised the RTP network limit to $10M on Feb 9 2025. Either PNC still applies a $1M cap or the page is stale. The chapter presents $1M as the RTP cap without making that distinction.
resolution: Keep $1M as PNC-stated with a note: network limit $10M since Feb 9 2025; PNC page may be stale.

claim: Consumer-facing RTP 'Real-Time Bill Pay' ... a capability most peers do not expose to consumers [S018]
finding: The capability is in the DSA (RFP appears in the Mobile app; cannot be cancelled once authorized). The gap-fill site search found no consumer marketing anywhere on pnc.com, and no peer comparison was sourced. 'Consumer-facing' and 'most peers do not' are not evidenced. Biller reach is also unknown.
resolution: Reworded strength (see patch).

claim: Wire pages publish no cutoffs, status tracking, cancellation/recall path or fraud-reimbursement stance [S010, S004]
finding: The gap-fill wire agreement (S905) gives processing hours (business days 8:30 a.m.-6:00 p.m. ET), a cancel/amend policy (no absolute right; best effort) and a 30-minute cancel for consumer international transfers. Only 'no status tracking' and 'no fraud-reimbursement stance' still hold, and weakness[8] already covers them.
resolution: Reworded weakness (see patch).

claim: Zelle is mobile-app only; no web Zelle send documented
finding: Test challenge: absence of documentation does not prove absence. Checked whether PNC Online Banking offers Zelle anywhere.
resolution: Original claim stands.

claim: fednow_send: true (THIRD_PARTY)
finding: PNC's own Oct 21 2025 release never says 'send'; it only says PNC joined FedNow and expanded instant payments capabilities. The API catalog names RTP but not FedNow.
resolution: fednow_send: true (THIRD_PARTY) stands.

claim: (absent) UPIC, ACH Debit Block, ACH Debit Authorization
finding: PNC's small-business Cash Management page names money-movement controls and receivables products that the chapter leaves out: Universal Payment Identification Code (UPIC), ACH Debit Block, ACH Debit Authorization, plus ACH Debit/ACH Credit, Wire Transfer Services, Integrated Receivables and 'PNC Remote Deposit'. UPIC (a masked receiving-account identifier for ACH credits) and the ACH debit filters are material to an ACH-fraud comparison.
resolution: Two new sub-products (PNC-P14-S08 UPIC; PNC-P13-S10 ACH Debit Block / ACH Debit Authorization).

claim: (absent) FirstBank acquisition
finding: PNC closed its $4.1B acquisition of FirstBank (Colorado/Arizona) on Jan 5 2026. About 780,000 customers and 95 branches had moved to PNC platforms (Zelle, Bill Pay, PNC Mobile) by June 2026. That is a major 2026 change in the money-movement footprint and the user base for the new app experience.
resolution: Add 2026-01-05 FirstBank acquisition and the June 2026 conversion to recent changes.

claim: (absent) Congressional scrutiny of PNC Zelle scam reimbursement
finding: On July 1 2025, Sens. Warren and Blumenthal and Rep. Waters wrote to PNC's CEO asking for Zelle scam data and reimbursement policies, including for social-media-originated scams. This is context for the scam-reimbursement exception path. No PNC response was found.
resolution: Add as a context entry in recent changes.

claim: Bill pay UI is fragmented into three variants (Bill Pay Dashboard; two 'Pay Bills Summary' experiences)
finding: The Online Bill Pay page documents two instruction paths ('Virtual Wallet and Cash Flow Insight Accountholders' vs 'Other PNC Accountholders'). The 'Bill Pay Dashboard' is the scheduling screen used in those flows and in the consumer FAQ. Whether that adds up to three distinct live UIs or two paths plus a shared dashboard is unclear, and the help text may be legacy.
resolution: Add an open question. Only an authenticated view of both account types would settle whether there are two or three live bill pay UIs.

claim: Open questions list includes first-wave items duplicated by later, more precise entries
finding: open_questions[0] duplicates [3] (scam interstitial), [1] duplicates [8] (legacy Virtual Wallet automations) and [2] duplicates [9] (Bill Pay pay-a-person). The duplicates inflate the gap count shown to executives.
resolution: Resolve open_questions[0],[1],[2] as superseded.

claim: description: 'PNC is one of the seven Paze founding banks'
finding: PNC's Paze page says only that seven of the nation's largest banks, including PNC, currently support Paze. It never says 'founding'. The fact is broadly right (Paze launched in 2023 with seven EWS owner banks), but the cited bank source does not carry it.
resolution: Reworded description (see patch).
